messages:
emily: Drafting a hardened rollout for private/on-prem bundles. Goals: zero-default egress, RBAC tighten for the cluster-provisioner, audit records signed before egressing, and KMS integration options that work for airgapped customers. Putting up the sketch for review.

rick: Please call out observability impact. If we block egress by default we risk metrics exporters losing scrape targets. Propose a small allowlist (monitoring + kms) and a sidecar annotation to opt-in extra endpoints.

emily: Agreed. Proposed sequence: 1) block egress default 2) deploy kms-proxy in control namespace 3) patch cluster-provisioner role to read-only for secrets/pods 4) enable audit-signer to sign with ephemeral wrapping key 5) canary a single shard.

anand: For RBAC: instead of patching in place, create new ClusterRole cluster-provisioner-limited and bind to provisioner SA in canary namespaces. That avoids rollbacks being painful. Example manifest: 
```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: cluster-provisioner-limited
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods","secrets"]
  verbs: ["get","list"]
```
Then ClusterRoleBinding to the provisioner serviceaccount only in canary.

rick: Netpol idea: use DNS-based egress via egress-gateway so we can allow FQDNs instead of raw IPs. For on-prem airgap fallback, allow only the kms-proxy service CIDR. Sample policy for the latter: 
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: egress-to-kms-proxy-only
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: ["Egress"]
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          edge: kms
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
Note: empty podSelector applies to all pods in the namespace, adjust accordingly.

emily: KMS integration modes: (A) Customer KMS endpoint reachable from cluster (mTLS + allowlisted host); (B) Local HSM connector that exposes a signing API on localhost and never talks outbound; (C) Hybrid where an offline HSM signs and we ship signed envelopes out. We should document acceptance criteria for each mode.

anand: Audit signing: logs should be hashed, signed, and include a signature header with key id + timestamp. We should rotate wrapping keys on a cadence and publish key fingerprints in the tenant attest report. Proposed TTL for ephemeral wrapping keys: 7 days.

emily: Vulnerability note: we discovered keystore-connector v0.9.1 uses an embedded SSH server with weak auth. We should block upgrade window until v0.9.4 is deployed. Can we automate a preflight that scans images for known CVEs?

anand: Yes — add container-scan step to the deploy pipeline (fail fast). For the canary apply, require passing SBOM + CVE check.

infra-bot: Alert created INC-2026-046: keystore-connector upgrade scheduled (owner: emily).

emily: Operational controls: add egress anomaly detector that looks for connections to non-allowlisted hosts and triggers an automated isolate pod (taint node or cordon) + alert to sec-oncall. Also store signed audit batches in an immutable object store (signed + checksummed).

rick: Rollback plan: 1) revert ClusterRoleBinding to previous role 2) remove netpols 3) revoke ephemeral wrapping keys 4) revert keystore-connector image. Keep runbook steps concise.

emily: Canary schedule: tonight 23:30 UTC. Checklist I'll follow: [create limited role + binding, deploy kms-proxy, apply netpol to canary ns, patch CI to require image scan, deploy signed-audit-forwarder, monitor egress + audit signatures for 1h, rotate wrap keys]. Anyone available for on-call?

anand: I can be on call.
rick: SG, I can jump in for metrics fallout.
emily: Thanks. I'll update the private-deploy runbook with manifests and add the HSM connector docs link. Will follow up with a brief post-canal report and indicators (egress anomalies, signature verification failures).
